summary.title: GitHub Monaspace Case Study
summary.one_liner: Learn how Lettermatic and GitHub Next designed Monaspace, an open-source superfamily of five monospace coding typefaces with Texture Healing, variable axes, and custom ligatures.
takeaways: Monaspace is a superfamily of five open-source monospace typefaces (Argon, Neon, Xenon, Radon, Krypton) that share one grid so they can be mixed.
Texture Healing is a context-aware feature that widens letters like m and w and narrows letters like i and l next to each other while keeping the monospace grid intact.
Variable axes for weight, width, and slant, plus alternate zeros, asterisks, and about 100 custom ligatures, allow personalization.
Typographic style can add a new dimension of emphasis to code beyond color-based syntax highlighting, which also supports accessibility for low vision and colorblind readers.
Version 1.4 added Cyrillic, Greek, and Vietnamese support, bringing the language count to just over 220.
summary.summary: This case study by Lettermatic describes its work with GitHub Next on Monaspace, a free, open-source superfamily of five monospace typefaces released in November 2023. It explains the history of monospace type, the design goals behind each face, and the Texture Healing technique that adjusts neighboring glyph widths within a fixed grid. It also covers personalization options (variable weight, width, and slant, zero and asterisk variants, ligature sets) and accessibility considerations, and notes the 1.4 update for Cyrillic, Greek, and Vietnamese.
